subject: Reserved commit term, staging guarantees, and start-window questions
messages:
-----Original Message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Cara Jensen <cara@helioslabs.com>, Maya Ortiz <maya.ortiz@helioslabs.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved commit term, staging guarantees, and start-window questions

Hi Cara / Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. As we discussed, I wanted to put our proposed structure in writing and surface a few open items so your legal/finance teams can evaluate.

High level proposal (Dedicated reserved commit):
- Term options: 12 / 24 / 36 months (we typically see best unit economics at 24+ months)
- Staging/onramp: phased ramp with an initial staging buffer (see attached capacity model)
- Throughput guarantee: committed sustained throughput for the GPU pool with explicit burst allowance
- Start window: customer selects target Start Date (SD). If we miss SD by >14 days, we provide a prorated credit for the delayed period.

Open items for HelioLabs to confirm:
1) Preferred term (you mentioned budget prefers shorter commit with extension option).
2) Acceptable ramp schedule (we can do 50% → 75% → 100% over first 6 months by default).
3) Any hard latency/throughput SLOs we should bake into the contract (99th %-ile latency vs sustained tokens/sec).
4) Billing preference: monthly invoice vs quarterly in arrears.

Attached: helioslabs_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (sample ramp + token throughput), helioslabs_forecast_q32026.xlsx

If you're comfortable, I can draft a term summary and pull in finance for a preliminary pricing deck (Icc: lauren). Otherwise, happy to hop on a 30-minute call tomorrow.

—
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147


On Thu, 30 Jul 2026 at 11:05 AM, Cara Jensen <cara@helioslabs.com> wrote:

> Hi Ben —
> 
> Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side (we've looped in Maya who owns procurement):
> 
> - Term preference: our finance team is pushing for a 12-month firm commit with an automatic option to extend to 24 months at a pre-agreed discount. They want flexibility if product usage doesn't ramp as fast as forecast.
> - Ramp expectations: HelioLabs would prefer a softer onramp — something like 30% → 60% → 90% over 6 months. We still need a staging buffer but want lower upfront cash flow.
> - SLOs: Our app is latency-sensitive. Can Redwood guarantee 95th %-ile infer latency for small-chat workloads under dedicated commits? If not a strict SLA, can we get performance profiles and fallbacks documented in the contract?
> - Credits: we are also sensitive to delayed start dates — any delay >30 days should trigger credit. Would you be open to a weekly credit cap until start?
> 
> Attached is our internal forecast and a short note from procurement: helioslabs_forecast_q32026.xlsx
> 
> We'll review a pricing summary if you can accommodate a modest staging concession for the first 60 days.
> 
> Best,
> Cara
> VP, Cloud Platform — HelioLabs
> cara@helioslabs.com


On Thu, 30 Jul 2026 at 14:20 Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:

> Hi Cara / Maya —
> 
> Appreciate the fast turnaround. Editable answers inline below and a concrete concessions proposal.
> 
> 1) Term: we can offer a 12-month firm commit plus an optional 12-month extension exercisable at month 9 at a pre-agreed discount rate. Alternatively, a 24-month firm commit gives a deeper unit discount (see attached commit_term_summary.pdf).
> 
> 2) Ramp: we can support your softer onramp. Proposed phased schedule for HelioLabs:
>    - Months 1–3: 30% of full committed capacity
>    - Months 4–6: 60% of full committed capacity
>    - Month 7+: 90% (we can bump to 100% if requested)
>    This schedule is reflected in helioslabs_capacity_model_v1.xlsx.
> 
> 3) Performance/SLOs: for dedicated reserved pools we provide performance profiles per model family. For small-chat workloads we can commit to a 95th %-ile infer latency target for the primary model family under normal operating load; the contract language will reference a measured test harness and define outages vs degraded performance. We also include automatic fallback to a lower-cost variant if capacity hotspots occur. For strict SLA language we gate credits on verified telemetry.
> 
> 4) Start-date delays & credits: we can grant a weekly prorated credit for start delays beyond 14 days up to a cap equal to two months' commit value. We can negotiate the exact cap in the term sheet.
> 
> Concessions proposal (to get you closer to procurement approval):
> - 10% one-time staging credit applied to first invoice (covers early overprovisioning)
> - Early-extension option (12→24) with pre-agreed 5% discount on months 13–24
> - DocuSign draft & HubSpot record to be shared after you confirm term selection (links below)
> 
> Next steps: I will draft a short term summary and pricing grid for the two paths (12+extension vs 24 firm) and loop in finance. Lauren — could you confirm the discount tiers and whether we can tighten the delay-credit cap to 6 weeks for this deal? Grace — can you validate the SLO wording we should present to legal?
> 
> Thanks,
> Ben
> 
> Attachments: commit_term_summary.pdf
> Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890, https://www.docusign.com/rooms/abc123


On Fri, 31 Jul 2026 at 15:48 Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:

> Team —
> 
> Quick internal summary before we send a revised term sheet to HelioLabs:
> - Offer both options: 12mo firm + extension OR 24mo firm. Pricing grid attached.
> - Approve the 10% staging credit on first invoice.
> - Delay credit: cap at 6 weeks of prorated monthly value (we'll present as "up to 6 weeks").
> - SLO language: Grace to provide baseline 95th %-ile target and the measured test harness wording.
> 
> Ben — if you can confirm the pricing grid numbers by EOD I'll prepare the redline. If HelioLabs is pushing for weekly credits beyond our cap, we'll push back and offer a 50% staging credit alternative.
> 
> -Lauren
> Director, Revenue Operations
> lauren_bishop@redwood.com
